title: </> htmx ~ Yes, and...
summary: A CS teacher argues programming remains a good career, but juniors must write code themselves, use AI as a tutor rather than a generator, and build communication, business and architecture skills.

assertions.quote: I do think AI is going to change computer programming. Not as dramatically as some people think, but in some

verdicts.note: Through 2026 evidence points to role change and slower junior hiring, not elimination of the profession; long-run is uncertain.

assertions.quote: If a junior programmer does not learn to write code and simply generates it, they are robbing

verdicts.note: Anthropic's 2026 RCT found AI-assisted learners scored lower on mastery of a new library, and other studies show reduced engagement; effects depend on how AI is used.

assertions.quote: Compilers are, for the most part, deterministic in a way that current AI tools are not.

verdicts.note: A historical framing; the analogy is debated because LLM output is non-deterministic, unlike compilers.

assertions.quote: significant accidental complexity by choosing inappropriate approaches to problems, taking shortcuts, etc.

verdicts.note: Code-bloat and duplication findings support a tendency toward verbose, over-engineered output, but it varies a lot by model and prompt.

assertions.quote: AI, used properly, is a tremendously effective TA.

verdicts.note: Anthropic's 2026 study found high scorers used AI for conceptual questions and explanations while low scorers delegated; small sample and a single learning task.

assertions.quote: the ability to write, think and communicate clearly, both with LLMs and humans seems likely to be much more

verdicts.note: Requirements, stakeholder alignment and judgment remain hard to delegate; plausible though not strictly testable.

assertions.quote: I think software architecture will become a more important skill over time

verdicts.note: Humans still own constraints and tradeoffs, but models can now propose reasonable designs when given context; the gap is narrowing.

assertions.quote: Senior programmers who already have a lot of experience from the pre-AI era are in a good spot to use LLMs effectively

verdicts.note: Experts get more reliable results and catch errors, but several RCTs show larger measured speedups for juniors, and METR found experts slowed; contested.

assertions.quote: Particularly dangerous is firing off prompts and then getting sucked into

verdicts.note: METR's screen recordings showed more idle/waiting time with AI and participants reported distraction; how much of the slowdown it explains is unquantified.

assertions.quote: The temptation to vibe your way through problems is very, very high, but you will need to fight against that temptation.

verdicts.note: Unreviewed AI-built apps commonly ship with security, scaling and maintainability problems; prototypes are their sweet spot.

assertions.quote: And companies: let the juniors write at least some of the code. It is in your interest.

verdicts.note: A straightforward pipeline argument made by IBM and others; the long-run effect is unmeasured yet but well reasoned.

assertions.quote: programmer job market tends to be cyclical with booms and busts

verdicts.note: The 2022-23 decline began before ChatGPT and tracks rate hikes and over-hiring; most economists attribute it mainly to macro factors, though AI may weigh on junior roles since 2024.
